newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada energy stocks resist stock market slide.
newsitem.headline: Canada energy stocks resist stock market slide.

text.p: Canada's oil and gas sector, buoyed by continuing high crude oil prices and a strong outlook for third-quarter earnings, was a bright light in Monday trade as most other sectors shed value.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's oil and gas index was up 3.68 points to 5,464.36, with stocks such as Talisman Energy Inc, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and Anderson Exploration Ltd posting strong gains.
Toronto's key TSE 300 index was off 6.21 points to 5281.20 in late trade after last week's string of record highs.
CIBC Woody Gundy analyst Peter Linder said his firm remained positive on oils and saw room for even higher stock prices despite their recent strong showing.
"The larger cap producers are still trading at or under six-times current year cash flow. So the stocks are not expensive," Linder said.
Energy shares would average seven or eight times cash flow in an overheated market, he said.
Linder said he expected several producers to show improved third-quarter results this year, thanks to strong oil production gains and high crude prices.

In the second quarter, a longer than expected spring breakup in western Canada put a lid on drilling for a large part of the period. But from July to September, companies struck back with a vengeance, keeping drilling rigs busy.
Linder said three firms -- Crestar Energy Inc, Renaissance Energy Ltd and Canadian Natural Resources Ltd -- were expected to show very strong results.

"They will have very strong oil production, coupled with great oil prices. These will be phenomenal third-quarter numbers -- much better than in the second quarter and much better than in the third quarter of '95," he said.
